question: What are the trunks made of?
html:
Our trunks are made from recycled plastic bottles, about 11 bottles per trunk. Across the brand, that adds up to about 26 million bottles recycled through 2021 (Fair Harbor public filings).

What we know

  • Main input: recycled plastic bottles, at about 11 bottles per trunk (Fair Harbor public filings).
  • Scale: about 26 million bottles in total through 2021 (Fair Harbor public filings).
  • Brand position: Fair Harbor is a public benefit corporation. Sustainability is central to the growth plan's goal of becoming a "year-round sustainable lifestyle brand" (Fair Harbor growth plan).
  • Implied sales: 26 million bottles at 11 per trunk suggests $60-80M in cumulative sales through 2021 (est., low confidence; Fair Harbor public filings).

What we can't confirm here

QuestionStatusWhat would answer it
Exact fabric blend (for example, recycled polyester share, spandex)Not in contextProduct spec sheets or care labels
Liner materialNot in contextProduct spec sheets
Whether non-swim lines use the same recycled inputsNot in contextSupplier bills of materials for the 64.0% of 372 live products that are non-swim
Bottles per trunk today vs. 2021Not updatedCurrent sourcing records

The bottle count dates to 2021. Newer ranges, including golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom launched in 2025-2026, may use different materials (Fair Harbor growth plan). We'd rather point you to the product page than guess.

Where to check

  • Each product page and the sewn-in care label list the fabric content for that style.
  • Customer support can confirm details for a specific style or size.

The recycled-bottle story underpins the brand's price point and its pitch to golf pro shops, campus bookstores and coastal specialty buyers, as the growth plan aims to take Fair Harbor from about 250 doors to about 520. That makes accurate, current material claims a margin and wholesale issue, not just a copy issue.

Next actions

  1. Pull current spec sheets. Collect fabric composition for all live products and publish it in a structured format on product pages, so this answer can cite exact blends.
  2. Refresh the bottle count. Confirm with sourcing whether "about 11 bottles per trunk" still holds, and update the cumulative figure past 2021.
  3. Map recycled content by category. Record which non-swim lines use recycled inputs, so wholesale reps and the fit and CX agents give consistent answers.
  4. Get claims reviewed. Send any public sustainability language to the company's own counsel before it goes into wholesale line sheets.
